questions.question: Select the most appropriate meaning of the underlined idiom in the following sentence. Sejal visits the nearby temple off and on .
questions.questionHtml:
Select the most appropriate meaning of the underlined idiom in the following sentence.
Sejal visits the nearby temple off and on.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is: Option 1.

Key Points

  • The idiom "off and on" means something that happens periodically, not continuously or regularly. (समय-समय पर)
    • Example: It rained off and on throughout the day.
  • "Periodically" refers to something that occurs at regular intervals of time. (समय-समय पर)
    • Example: The company conducts performance reviews periodically to ensure employee growth.
  • Hence, we can infer that the idiom "off and on" means "periodically".

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

Here are the other options explained along with their Hindi meanings and example sentences:

  • Constantly (लगातार): Continuously over a period of time.
    • Example: He was constantly checking his phone for messages.
  • Continuously (लगातार): Without interruption or end.
    • Example: The river flowed continuously through the valley.
  • Regularly (नियमित रूप से): At consistent, recurring intervals.
    • Example: She visits her grandparents regularly every weekend.

questions.question: Parts of a sentence are given below in jumbled order. Select the option that arranges the parts in the correct sequence to form a meaningful sentence. (P) unlock their potential (Q) empowers individuals to (O) and shape their future (R) the power of education
questions.questionHtml:
Parts of a sentence are given below in jumbled order. Select the option that arranges the parts in the correct sequence to
form a meaningful sentence.
(P) unlock their potential
(Q) empowers individuals to
(O) and shape their future
(R) the power of education
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Option (3) i.e. RQPO
Key Points
  • The sentence logically starts with "The power of education," which is correctly indicated by part (R).
  • Following this, "empowers individuals to" (Q) continues the statement, explaining what the power of education does.
  • "Unlock their potential" (P) follows logically, detailing the first action that education empowers individuals to do.
  • Ending with, "and shape their future" (O) completes the sentence by adding the second action that education enables.
Therefore, the correct answer is RQPO.
Additional Information
  • Option 1 (QROP): This option starts with "empowers individuals to" which is missing a subject to complete the sentence.
  • Option 2 (OPRQ): This option starts with "and shape their future" without specifying "the power of education," making it incomplete and grammatically incorrect.
  • Option 4 (RPOQ): This option places "unlock their potential" before "empowers individuals to," which disrupts the logical flow of the sentence.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the underlined word in the following sentence. The teammates made several jibes at the opponent team members during the interview.
questions.questionHtml:
Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the underlined word in the following sentence.
The teammates made several jibes at the opponent team members during the interview.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is: Consolation.

Key Points

  • The word "jibes" means mocking or taunting remarks. (मज़ाक उड़ाना)
    • Example: The kids exchanged jibes during the game.
  • "Consolation" refers to comfort received by a person after a loss or disappointment. (सांत्वना)
    • Example: She found consolation in the kind words of her friends after losing the match.
  • Hence, we can infer that the opposite of 'jibes' is 'consolation'.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Consolation.

Additional Information

Here are the other options explained along with their Hindi meanings and example sentences:

  • Mockery (मज़ाक): Teasing and contemptuous language or behavior directed at a particular person or thing.
    • Example: His mockery of her accent was hurtful.
  • Inspiration (प्रेरणा): The process of being mentally stimulated to do or feel something, especially to do something creative.
    • Example: Her speech was a great source of inspiration to the students.
  • Contradict (विरोधाभास): Deny the truth of (a statement) by asserting the opposite.
    • Example: The witness's statements contradict each other.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. Athens was suffering under the rule of a powerful small group that had no concern for the people’s welfare.
questions.questionHtml:
Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence.
Athens was suffering under the rule of a powerful small group that had no concern for the people’s welfare.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is: Option 2.

Key Points

  • The word "democracy" means a system of government where the citizens exercise power by voting. (लोकतंत्र)
    • Example: The country is a democracy, where every citizen has a right to vote.
  • "oligarchy" refers to a small group of people having control of a country or organization. (कुलीनतंत्र)
    • Example: The nation was ruled by an oligarchy that controlled all aspects of life.
  • Hence, the correct term for a powerful small group that had no concern for the people's welfare is 'oligarchy'.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

Here are the other options explained along with their Hindi meanings and example sentences:

  • Democracy (लोकतंत्र): A system of government by the whole population, typically through elected representatives.
    • Example: India is the world's largest democracy.
  • Monarchy (राजशाही): A form of government with a monarch at the head.
    • Example: The United Kingdom is a constitutional monarchy.
  • Missionary (धर्मप्रचारक): A person sent on a religious mission, especially one sent to promote Christianity in a foreign country.
    • Example: The missionary worked in remote villages to spread the teachings of his faith.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate option that can rectify the incorrectly spelt word in the following sentence. I doubt that these lifts can accomodate 100 people.

  • "accomodate" is an incorrect spelling and does not carry any specific meaning. (गलत वर्तनी)
    • Example: This room can accomodate all the guests. (Incorrect spelling)

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. 'accommodate'.

Additional Information

Here are the other options explained along with their Hindi meanings and example sentences:

  • acomodate (गलत वर्तनी): Incorrect spelling of 'accommodate'.
    • Example: This room can acomodate all the guests. (Incorrect spelling)
  • accommodatte (गलत वर्तनी): Incorrect spelling of 'accommodate'.
    • Example: The hall can accommodatte a large number of people. (Incorrect spelling)
  • accomondate (गलत वर्तनी): Incorrect spelling of 'accommodate'.
    • Example: The venue can accomondate all the participants. (Incorrect spelling)

questions.question: Select the sentence that is expressed in passive voice.
questions.questionHtml: Select the sentence that is expressed in passive voice.

options.text: Children are participating in sand-art competition.
options.html: Children are participating in sand-art competition.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is Option 4.
 
Key Points
  • Passive voice structure: The object of the active voice sentence becomes the subject of the passive voice sentence.
  • In this case, "the consignment" (the subject) is receiving the action (delivered).
  • The doer of the action is not mentioned in the sentence, and the focus is on what happened to the consignment.
  • This is a clear example of passive voice because the action is being done to the subject (the consignment), not by it.
  • The sentence "The consignment was delivered yesterday" focuses on the consignment being acted upon, not on who delivered it.
Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.
 
Correct Sentence: "The consignment was delivered yesterday."
 
Additional Information
  • Option 1: "I prefer tea to coffee." – This sentence is in active voice. The subject "I" is performing the action (prefer), and "tea" and "coffee" are objects of the preference.
  • Option 2: "Children are participating in sand-art competition." – This sentence is in active voice. The subject "children" are performing the action (participating). "In sand-art competition" is the location of the action. 
  • Option 3: "She sketches beautifully." – This sentence is in active voice. The subject "she" is performing the action (sketches).

questions.question: Select the most appropriate meaning of the underlined idiom. This year’s budget is unlikely to pass as law since the president’s proposed budgets typically face a jaundiced eye , but this one has gotten even more scepticism.
questions.questionHtml:
Select the most appropriate meaning of the underlined idiom.
This year’s budget is unlikely to pass as law since the president’s proposed budgets typically face a jaundiced eye, but this one has gotten even more scepticism.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is: Option 3.

Key Points

  • The word "jaundiced eye" means a view or attitude that is characterized by cynicism, skepticism, or suspicion. (संदेहपूर्ण दृष्टि)
    • Example: The committee viewed the proposal with a jaundiced eye, questioning every detail.
  • "Resentment" refers to a feeling of anger or displeasure about someone or something unfair. (नाराज़गी)
    • Example: She felt a deep resentment towards her boss for not acknowledging her hard work.
  • Hence, we can infer that "jaundiced eye" relates to skepticism or cynicism, which aligns with "resentment".

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

Here are the other options explained along with their Hindi meanings and example sentences:

  • Jealousy (ईर्ष्या): A feeling of envy towards someone due to their achievements or advantages.
    • Example: Her jealousy over her friend's success caused a rift in their relationship.
  • Confidence (आत्मविश्वास): A feeling or belief that one can rely on someone or something; firm trust.
    • Example: His confidence in his abilities helped him secure the job.
  • Good will (सद्भावना): A friendly, helpful, or cooperative attitude or feeling.
    • Example: The company's good will towards its employees is evident in its generous benefits package.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the underlined word in the given sentence. Her behaviour was so ostentatious that it attracted the attention of everyone in the room.

Here are the other options explained along with their Hindi meanings and example sentences:

  • Repulsive (घृणित): Arousing intense distaste or disgust.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the underlined word. Her remarks were relevant to the discussion.

  • "Inappropriate" refers to something that is not suitable or proper in the circumstances. (अनुचित)
    • Example: Wearing casual clothes to a formal event is considered inappropriate.
  • Hence, we can infer that the opposite of 'relevant' is 'inappropriate'.

Here are the other options explained along with their Hindi meanings and example sentences:

questions.question: Select the option that can be used as a one-word substitute for the given group of words. The evening time when the sun has just set and it is almost dark.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate answer for blank number 1.
questions.questionHtml: Select the most appropriate answer for blank number 1.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is 'assessment'.
 
Key Points
  • The Human Development Index (HDI) is described as a summary measure of accomplishments.
  • 'Assessment' means the evaluation or estimation of the nature, quality, or ability of someone or something, which fits the context.
  • Other options like 'regiment,' 'involvement,' and 'collect' do not appropriately describe the HDI in this context.
    • 'Regiment' typically refers to a military unit or a strict order, which is not suitable.
    • 'Involvement' means participation, which does not fit the context of a summary measure.
    • 'Collect' means to gather things together, which is unrelated to a measure or evaluation.
Therefore, the correct answer is 'Option 2'.
 
Complete Passage: The Human Development Index (HDI) is a summary assessment of average accomplishment in important areas of human development. Including living a long and healthy life, being informed and having a good quality of living. The HDI is the geometric mean of the normalized indices for each dimension. The health component is measured by life expectancy at birth, while the education dimension is measured by the average number of years of schooling for individuals aged 25 and above, as well as the expected number of years of schooling for school-age children.
 
Additional Information
  • Regiment (अनुशासन/विशेष व्यवस्था): Refers to a military unit or a strict order, not suitable for describing HDI.
  • Involvement (शामिल होना): Means participation, which does not fit the context of HDI as a measure.
  • Collect (संग्रह करना): Means to gather things together, which is unrelated to a summary measure or evaluation.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate answer for blank number 2.
questions.questionHtml: Select the most appropriate answer for blank number 2.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is 'including'.
 
Key Points
  • The passage explains that the HDI measures various aspects of human development life.
  • 'Including' is the correct choice as it shows that these aspects are part of the HDI measurements.
  • Other options like 'segregating,' 'exaggerating,' and 'manifesting' do not fit the context.
    • 'Segregating' means separating, which is not applicable.
    • 'Exaggerating' means overstating or describing something as greater than it is, which is inappropriate here.
    • 'Manifesting' means showing or displaying, which does not fit the idea of listing components.
Therefore, the correct answer is 'Option 3'.
 
Complete Passage: The Human Development Index (HDI) is a summary assessment of average accomplishment in important areas of human development.
